draft.title: Franchises
card: A franchise is a way of running a business. The owner pays another company to use its name, products and way of operating.
the company that owns the name and system and lets others use them.
the business owner who pays to use the franchisor's name and system.
Fast food chains are often franchises. Customers see a well-known name, and the franchisee follows the franchisor's methods.
draft.remember: A franchisee pays a franchisor to run a business under its name and system.

a.q: Sam pays a well-known pizza company to open a shop using its name and recipes. What is Sam?
opts: A franchisee
A franchisor
A shareholder
A sole trader
a.why: Sam pays another company to use its name and way of operating, so Sam is the franchisee. The pizza company that owns the name and recipes is the franchisor.
a.clue: Who pays, and who is paid?

b.q: Priya wants to open a shop. Which choice would make it a franchise?
opts: Paying a juice company to sell under its name and methods
Naming the shop after her own favourite juice
Borrowing money from a bank to buy shop fittings
Hiring staff who have worked in other juice shops
b.why: A franchise means paying another company to use its name and way of operating. Naming a shop herself, borrowing money or hiring experienced staff does not involve using another company's system.
b.clue: Look for paying to use another company's name.

b.best: Paying a juice company to sell under its name and methods

problems.detail: Many franchisees are sole traders. Nothing in the stem says Sam is not the only owner, so 'A sole trader' is also defensible. Add a detail that rules it out, or replace that distractor.

the company that owns the name and system and lets others use them.

a.q: Sam pays a well-known pizza company to open a shop using its name and recipes. Which is correct?
opts: Sam is the franchisee, the company is the franchisor
Sam is the franchisor, the company is the franchisee
Sam and the company are both franchisors
Sam and the company are both franchisees
a.why: Sam pays to use another company's name and way of operating, so Sam is the franchisee. The pizza company owns the name and recipes and lets Sam use them, so it is the franchisor. Swapping the two roles is the most common mistake.
a.clue: Who pays, and who is paid?

b.q: Priya wants to open a juice shop. Which choice would make it a franchise?
opts: Paying a juice company to sell under its name and methods
Naming the shop after her own favourite juice
Borrowing money from a bank to buy shop fittings
Hiring staff who have worked in other juice shops
b.why: A franchise means paying another company to use its name and way of operating. Borrowing from a bank also involves another business, but the bank does not give Priya a name or a system to follow. Naming the shop herself or hiring experienced staff keeps it her own business.
b.clue: Think about whose name would be above the door.
